reason: Throughout this passage (Exodus 7-12), Pharaoh, the primary leader figure responsible for the Hebrew people's enslavement, repeatedly fails to take accountability for their condition. While he temporarily admits sin after certain plagues (חָטָאתִי - 'I have sinned'), he consistently refuses to act on his words and release the Israelites. He says 'לְכוּ עִבְדוּ אֶת־ יְהוָה' (Go, worship the Lord) but then 'וְלֹא שִׁלַּח אֶת־ הָעָם' (and would not send the people). God explicitly states that He hardened Pharaoh's heart multiple times ('וַיְחַזֵּק יְהוָה אֶת־ לֵב פַּרְעֹה'), showing Pharaoh's fundamental refusal of responsibility. He continues holding the Hebrews in bondage despite catastrophic plagues affecting his own nation, demonstrating a complete abdication of accountability for their suffering and enslaved status.
